title: Colour Palettes
text: Display colour swatches palette: n fixes many colours palette contributes, following rules pal_get(). max_colors still caps many drawn:
code: pal_show("Paired") pal_show("Set1") # Take 3 colours from each palette pal_show(c("Set1", "lancet", "Dark2"), n = 3)  # More colours than the palette holds are interpolated (Set1 only has 9) pal_show("Set1", n = 12)  # Colour vectors take `n` too, and keep their names as labels pal_show(pal_paraSC, n = 6)

code: x <- factor(c("I", "II", "III", "IV"))  # Recode by name fct_cat(x, early = c("I", "II"), late = c("III", "IV")) #> [1] early early late  late  #> Levels: early late  # Recode by position fct_cat(x, g1 = 1:2, g2 = 3:4) #> [1] g1 g1 g2 g2 #> Levels: g1 g2

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
text: examples build base plot:
code: p <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, color = Species)) +   geom_point(size = 2) p

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
text: Chain multiple formatting operations one call:
code: p |> fmt_plot(   fmt_legend_list = list(legend.position = "bottom"),   fmt_tag_list = list(labels = "A") ) + theme(text = element_text(size = 14))

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
text: Labels follow data plots nested patchworks, skipping spacers, guide areas insets. Automatic labels continue Z AA, AB, . Calling fmt_tag() replaces earlier tags keeping user annotations. Inside faceted plot label appears facet; outside tag appears whole plot. Inside-styling fill alpha passed ggpp::geom_label_npc() ....
code: p |> fmt_tag("A") p |> fmt_tag("B", label_position = c(0.95, 0.95), size = 16) outside <- fmt_tag(p, "A", label_position = "tl-out",                    label.padding = grid::unit(0.3, "lines")) outside fmt_tag(outside, "B", label_position = "br")

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
code: p |> fmt_legend(position = "bottom", direction = "horizontal")

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
code: p |> fmt_ref(x = 5.8, y = 3.0) # Multiple lines with colours p |> fmt_ref(x = c(5, 6, 7), color = c("red", "blue", "green"))

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
text: FALSE retains current axes restore elements hidden earlier. single plot, TRUE hides selected axis. container, explicit indices count editable plots recursively, excluding spacers, guide areas, insets fixed wrapped graphics.  plot_dims takes precedence manual selectors. Lists use supplied grid dimensions; patchworks follow existing positions, including empty cells, nesting spanning design areas. hides decoration : make different scales identical. flat patchworks matching axes, patchwork::plot_layout(axes = "collect", axis_titles = "collect") also available. Format ggplot wrapping wrap_elements().
code: # Hide x-axis (useful for multi-panel layouts) p |> fmt_axis(x.axis = TRUE) p_grid <- patchwork::wrap_plots(p, p, p, p, nrow = 2, byrow = FALSE) fmt_axis(p_grid, plot_dims = c(2, 2))

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
code: p_facet <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width)) +   geom_point() +   facet_wrap(~Species)  p_facet |> fmt_strip(label_fill = c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A"))

code: p |> fmt_bg(palette = "Paired", alpha = 0.1)

code: p |> fmt_scale(x = list(limits = c(4, 8)),                y = list(limits = c(2, 4.5)))

code: p_violin <- ggplot(iris, aes(Species, Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +   geom_violin() p_violin |> fmt_boxplot()

title: ggplot2 Formatting: fmt_* and Themes
text: flatten_patchwork() function original name. Returns patchwork ordinary grid cells one level. Overall annotations collection settings retained; dimensions design rebuilt supplied layout arguments. Insets stay main plot, free() containers remain intact. Selection indices count protected groups one cell, well ordinary plots, spacers, guide areas wrapped graphics.
code: library(patchwork) nested <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4) flat <- fmt_flatten(nested, ncol = 2, axis_titles = "collect")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
code: library(UtilsR) library(ggplot2)  set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   Type  = factor(sample(c("A","B","C"), 200, TRUE, c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2))),   Group = factor(sample(c("X","Y","Z"), 200, TRUE)),   Batch = factor(sample(c("B1","B2"), 200, TRUE)) ) df$Region <- factor(ifelse(df$Group %in% c("X","Y"), "R1", "R2")) head(df) #>   Type Group Batch Region #> 1    A     Y    B2     R1 #> 2    A     X    B2     R1 #> 3    B     Y    B1     R1 #> 4    C     Y    B1     R1 #> 5    A     Y    B1     R1 #> 6    C     Z    B1     R2

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: common type. Supports stat = "percent" (default) "count", position = "stack" (default) "dodge".
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar") plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar",         stat = "count", position = "dodge", label = TRUE) plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar",         flip = TRUE, label = TRUE)

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: group.omitted, stat.level becomes bar:
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "bar", stat = "count",         label = TRUE, legend.position = "none")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: Use bg.dodge mode add alternating background colour bands. bg.must superset group.(group belongs exactly one bg level).
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar",         position = "dodge", bg.by = "Region") plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar",         position = "dodge", bg.by = "Region",         bg_palette = c("lightblue", "lightyellow"),         title = "Custom Background Colors")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: bar chart polar coordinates (theta = "x"). Good cyclical data.
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "rose") plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "rose",         stat = "count", position = "dodge")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: pie chart hole center. Supports dodge grouped spiral display.
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "ring", label = TRUE) plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "ring",         stat = "count", position = "dodge")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "pie", label = TRUE) plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "pie",         palette = "Paired",         title = "Type Distribution",         subtitle = "n = 200",         legend.position = "bottom",         legend.direction = "horizontal")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: Combines stepped area background bar overlay. Best showing trends across ordered groups.
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "trend", stat = "count") plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "trend",         stat = "count", label = TRUE)

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: Stacked area chart. Uses continuous x-axis internally.
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "area", stat = "count") plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "area",         stat = "count", position = "dodge")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: Bubble-style dot plot size encodes value.
code: plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "dot") plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "dot",         label = TRUE, stat = "count")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide
text: Requires stat.>= 2 column names. Shows flow categories.
code: plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group"), type = "sankey") plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group", "Batch"), type = "sankey")

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide

title: plt_cat: Unified Categorical Plot Guide

title: Utility Functions for Data Exploration and System Diagnostics
text: plt_cat() – One function, 11 chart types (bar, pie, ring, rose, dot, trend, area, sankey, chord, venn, upset), 27+ parameters plt_con() – One function, 4 chart types (violin, box, bar, dot) statistical comparisons, overlays, split/stack layout lv() – Instant variable summary data.frame Seurat objects grouping cross-tabulation fmt_*() – Chainable ggplot2 formatting: axes, tags, legends, reference lines, strips, comparisons, backgrounds, scales, 260 built-palettes via pal_get() / pal_list(), plus 11 hand-picked palettes (pal_lancet, pal_ditto, pal_igv, …) fct_cat() – Recode, reorder, reverse, binarise, group, combine factors one call

title: Utility Functions for Data Exploration and System Diagnostics
code: library(UtilsR)  set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   Type  = factor(sample(c("A","B","C"), 200, TRUE)),   Group = factor(sample(c("X","Y","Z"), 200, TRUE)),   Batch = factor(sample(c("B1","B2"), 200, TRUE)) )  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar")                           # stacked percent plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar",         stat = "count", position = "dodge", label = TRUE)            # dodged count plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "pie", label = TRUE)                     # pie chart plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "ring",         stat = "count", position = "dodge")                          # donut chart plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "rose")                         # rose (wind rose) plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "dot")                          # Cleveland dot plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "trend", stat = "count")        # trend line plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "area", stat = "count")         # area chart  # Multi-variable: sankey, chord, venn, upset plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group"), type = "sankey") plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group"), type = "chord") plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group"), type = "venn", stat_level = c("A", "X")) plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group"), type = "upset", stat_level = c("A", "X"))  # Split by facet + background bands plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", split.by = "Batch", type = "bar")

title: Utility Functions for Data Exploration and System Diagnostics
code: set.seed(1) df2 <- data.frame(   value = rnorm(200),   score = rnorm(200, mean = 2),   group = factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), 200, TRUE)),   batch = factor(sample(c("B1", "B2"), 200, TRUE)) )  # Basic types plt_con(df2, "value", "group")                          # violin (default) plt_con(df2, "value", "group", type = "box")            # boxplot plt_con(df2, "value", "group", type = "bar")            # mean +/- SD plt_con(df2, "value", "group", type = "dot")            # bubble dot plot  # Overlays plt_con(df2, "value", "group", add_box = TRUE, add_point = TRUE)  # Statistical comparisons plt_con(df2, "value", "group",         comparisons = list(c("A", "B"), c("A", "C")))  # Multiple features + stack plt_con(df2, c("value", "score"), "group", stack = TRUE)  # Split by batch plt_con(df2, "value", "group", split.by = "batch")

code: # --- Bar mode (stacked) --- set.seed(42) bar_df <- data.frame(   celltype = rep(c("T cell", "B cell", "NK cell", "Macrophage"),                  each = 2, times = 2),   response = rep(c("Risk", "Protective"), times = 8),   count    = sample(1:15, 16, replace = TRUE),   group    = rep(c("PHPT", "SHPT"), each = 8) ) PlotButterfly(bar_df, stat.by = "celltype", fill.by = "response",               value.by = "count", group.by = "group")   # --- Bar mode sorted by mean value (ascending) --- PlotButterfly(bar_df, stat.by = "celltype", fill.by = "response",               value.by = "count", group.by = "group", levels = "up")   # --- Bar dodge mode (side-by-side) --- PlotButterfly(bar_df, type = "bar_dodge", stat.by = "celltype",               fill.by = "response", value.by = "count",               group.by = "group",               palette = c("#E74C3C", "#3498DB"))   # --- Violin mode --- set.seed(123) dl <- data.frame(A = rnorm(40, 0.7, 0.2), B = rnorm(40, 0.3, 0.1)) dr <- data.frame(A = rnorm(40, 0.3, 0.15), B = rnorm(40, 0.7, 0.2)) PlotButterfly(type = "violin", data.left = dl, data.right = dr,               left.title = "Condition A", right.title = "Condition B") #> Warning: Vectorized input to `element_text()` is not officially supported. #> ℹ Results may be unexpected or may change in future versions of ggplot2.   # Violin with reference line and custom colours PlotButterfly(type = "violin", data.left = dl, data.right = dr,               left.title = "Group A", right.title = "Group B",               palette = c("#66a686", "#5292c4"),               ref.line = 0.25, add_point = TRUE) #> Warning: Vectorized input to `element_text()` is not officially supported. #> ℹ Results may be unexpected or may change in future versions of ggplot2.

title: Circular Lollipop Chart — PlotCircleLollipop
text: data data.frame least three columns: group, feature name, numeric value. Missing group labels rejected drawing. Unused group levels omitted chart. group_col Column name grouping variable. Default "group". name_col Column name feature names. Default "name". value_col Column name numeric scores. Default "value". top_n Integer. NULL, keep top top_n features per group ranked value_col (descending). Applied plotting. NULL = use rows -. value_scale Per-group value scaling applied top_n selection. Three options: "none" (default) scaling; values used -    normalised [0, 1] globally fall outside     range. constant global range outside [0, 1] uses     minimum lollipop height 0.05. "group" Scale group independently [0, 1]     using group's full value range original data     (top_n filtering). Max value group = 1, min = 0.     Preserves relative differences within group across whole     feature set. "top_n" Scale group independently [0, 1]     using displayed (post-top_n) values. Top displayed     feature = 1, bottom displayed feature = 0. Maximises visual spread     within sector. Extreme finite ranges rescaled subtraction avoid overflow. group_levels Character vector controlling display order groups. NULL = data appearance order (factor levels already factor). Must include every observed group; unobserved levels omitted. common_color Colour features shared across \(\geq 2\) groups. Default "#4682B4". unique_color Colour group-unique features. Default "#FF7F50". color_col Optional column name supplying per-row colours. provided, common_color / unique_color ignored. show_links Logical. Draw inner arcs connecting shared features across groups. Default TRUE. link_color Colour inner arcs. Default "#4e6a74". link_lwd Line width arcs. Default 0.5. link_h Bezier height arcs (0–1). Default 0.7. show_labels Logical. Draw feature name labels. Default TRUE. label_side place feature labels relative sector ring. Three options: "inside" (default) Labels narrow band     sector ring inner edge lollipop outer edge. Best small     datasets (groups / features per group). "outside" Labels inside grey sector boxes,     lollipop stems. Matches style Fig. 4 Lancet     Digital Health. Recommended 5–10 features per group. "outer" Labels placed beyond outer boundary     grey sector boxes, extending outward circle. Sector boxes     move one ring inward. Recommended large datasets     (> 10 features per group). label_cex Text size labels. Default 0.7. label_height Height label connector lines mm. Default 4. point_cex Size lollipop dots. Default 0.8. line_lwd Width lollipop stems. Default 1. sector_bg Background colour sector label track. Default "grey90". sector_cex Text size sector labels. Default 0.8. track_height Height lollipop track (0–1). Default 0.37. gap_after Gap angle (degrees) last sector. Default 20. gap_between Gap angle (degrees) sectors. text: data Input data one following formats: data.frame Must contain columns specified name_col     value_col.  group_col exists, faceted     multi-panel plot produced. Named numeric vector Values scores; names feature     labels.  Produces single-panel plot. Matrix Rows = features, columns = groups (e.g. cell types).     Use groups select specific columns. Scores must one-dimensional real numeric values. Numeric haven labelled scores supported, class-defined missing values (including SPSS user missings) excluded ranking. Matrix list columns, integer64, time classes complex scores supported; convert explicitly choosing units checking precision. group_col Column name grouping variable (e.g. cell type). Default "cell_type".  Ignored vector / matrix input. name_col Column name feature names. Default "gene".  Ignored vector / matrix input. value_col Column name numeric scores. Default "importance".  Ignored vector / matrix input. groups Character vector groups plot (matrix data.frame input).  NULL (default) = groups. Groups without non-missing scores skipped. error raised valid scores remain group selection. group_levels Character vector specifying display order. NULL = data appearance order factor levels. top_n Integer. Number top-ranked features highlight per group. Default 5. max_show Integer. Maximum features display per panel. Default 200. value_scale Per-group score scaling strategy. Three options: "none" (default) scaling; raw scores plotted -. "group" Scale group independently [0, 1]     using group's full value range original data     (max_show truncation). Useful absolute score     magnitudes differ greatly across groups. "top_n" Scale group [0, 1] using     displayed (post-max_show) values. Stretches visible range     within panel maximise visual separation. Extreme finite ranges rescaled subtraction avoid overflow. highlight_color Colour top-ranked points. Default "#007D9B". base_color Colour remaining points. Default "#BECEE3". label_size Numeric. Text label size. Default 4. point_size Numeric. Point size. Default 3. title Character. Plot title. NULL = auto. ylab Character. Y-axis label. Default "Importance". base_size Numeric. Base font size. Default 12. ncol Integer. Number columns faceted layout. Default 4. clean_names Logical. Strip common prefixes (HALLMARK_, KEGG_, etc.) replace underscores spaces. Default TRUE. return_type return: "plot" (default), "data" (ranked data.frame), "". filename Output file path. NULL = save. width Output width inches. Default 12. height Output height inches. title: Rank Correlation Scatter Plot — PlotRankCor
text: data Data frame long format. Must contain columns specified stat., value., group., method.. stat.Character. Column name category labels (e.g. cell type). Labels shown via geom_text_repel. value.Character. Column name numeric score used compute ranks. Ranks computed rank(-score) (descending) within group.x method.combination. Missing scores remain missing contribute correlation. Duplicate categories averaged ranking individual observations. Spearman tests use approximate p-values (exact = FALSE). Numeric labelled scores respect declared missing values. Stored integer64 scores require bit64; ranks preserve integer precision, raw scores mapped aesthetics must within +/-2^53. group.Character. Column name grouping / faceting variable (e.g. comparison). level gets facet panel. NULL, data treated single group (faceting). Missing groups retained "<NA>"; suffix distinguishes label existing group names. method.Character. Column name identifying two methods. Must exactly 2 observed, non-missing levels. Factor levels determine order; vectors use first appearance. first maps x-axis second y-axis. use_rank Logical. TRUE (default), plot ranks compute Spearman correlation. FALSE, plot raw values compute Pearson correlation. Raw-value tests use finite pairs; fewer three usable pairs constant vector yield missing correlation statistics. scale_x Character. Scaling method x-axis values (use_rank = FALSE). One "none" (default), "minmax", "zscore", "log1p", "rank". Applied per group. Scaling preserves missing values. Constant observed values map zero; z-scores fewer two observed values remain missing. Non-finite raw values become missing scaling transformation. scale_y Character. Scaling method y-axis values (use_rank = FALSE). options scale_x. size_by Character NULL. Column name numeric variable map point size. column values aggregated (mean) across two methods per stat x group combination. continuous size scale added plot. Default NULL (points use fixed pt.size). warning reports mapped columns finite category/group means; missing mapping retained. size_range Numeric vector length 2. Range point sizes size_by specified. Default c(1, 6). alpha_by Character NULL. Column name numeric variable map point transparency (alpha), producing colour-depth effect – darker points indicate higher values. Values aggregated (mean) across two methods per stat x group combination. Overrides fixed alpha. Similar alpha.PlotButterfly. Default NULL (uniform alpha). alpha_range Numeric vector length 2. Output alpha range alpha_by mapping. Default c(0.3, 1). palette Named unnamed character vector colours group.levels. Default NULL uses c("#B2182B", "#2166AC", ...) pal_lancet. Named colours must cover every observed group. default palette interpolated groups available colours. pt.size Numeric. Point size (used size_by = NULL). Default 3. alpha Numeric 0–1. Point transparency (used alpha_by = NULL). Default 0.8. label.size Numeric. Label text size. Default 3. max.overlaps Integer. Maximum overlapping labels passed geom_text_repel. Default 20. show.label Logical. Whether display text labels. Default TRUE. show.diag Logical. Whether show diagonal reference line (y = x). Default TRUE. title Character. Plot title. Default NULL (auto-generated). xlab Character. X-axis label. Default NULL (auto). ylab Character. Y-axis label. Default NULL (auto). base_size Numeric. Base font size. Default 13. legend.position Legend position. Default "none". omitted, size alpha mapping automatically shows inside legend. Explicit "none" always hides legend. width Numeric. Output width inches. Default 12. height Numeric. Output height inches. Default 6. filename Character. File path save plot. Default NULL (saving).

code: set.seed(42) df <- data.frame(   cell_type  = rep(LETTERS[1:8], times = 4),   score      = runif(32, 0, 1),   pvalue     = runif(32, 0, 0.1),   comparison = rep(rep(c("PHPT", "SHPT"), each = 8), 2),   method     = rep(c("scMMR", "miloR"), each = 16) )  # Basic usage PlotRankCor(df, stat.by = "cell_type", value.by = "score",             group.by = "comparison", method.by = "method") #>   group     rho      P #>   ──────────────────── #>   PHPT   -0.071  0.867 #>   SHPT    0.119  0.779   # With size mapping PlotRankCor(df, stat.by = "cell_type", value.by = "score",             group.by = "comparison", method.by = "method",             size_by = "score", legend.position = "right") #>   group     rho      P #>   ──────────────────── #>   PHPT   -0.071  0.867 #>   SHPT    0.119  0.779   # With alpha depth (darker = higher score) PlotRankCor(df, stat.by = "cell_type", value.by = "score",             group.by = "comparison", method.by = "method",             alpha_by = "score") #>   group     rho      P #>   ──────────────────── #>   PHPT   -0.071  0.867 #>   SHPT    0.119  0.779   # Combined: size + alpha depth PlotRankCor(df, stat.by = "cell_type", value.by = "score",             group.by = "comparison", method.by = "method",             size_by = "score", alpha_by = "pvalue",             legend.position = "right") #>   group     rho      P #>   ──────────────────── #>   PHPT   -0.071  0.867 #>   SHPT    0.119  0.779

what: Impute Missing Values with Weighted K-Nearest Neighbours — impute_na_knn
title: Impute Missing Values with Weighted K-Nearest Neighbours — impute_na_knn
text: Impute missing values mixed-type data kNN. Labelled variables temporarily converted factors distance calculation, restored original storage type, variable label, value labels, attributes. SPSS user-missing codes treated missing rather donor categories. Labelled missingness interpreted even haven loaded. Labelled donor values restored original category values, without parsing rounded printed numbers. Stored integer64 columns require bit64. imputation needed, observed values must within +/-2^53 exact numeric conversion. Imputed values converted back integer64 storage, fractional parts truncated. Ordinary integer columns also retain truncation toward zero converting weighted means back integer storage. VIM's distance weights aggregation rules retained. Degenerate weights use equal weights selected neighbours. Wholly missing rows retained without imputation, remaining missing values reported. Infinite numeric input rejected imputation needed. Dates, date-times, time differences durations use numeric distances retain original classes, time zones units. Calendar periods intervals, complex vectors raw vectors require explicit conversion imputation.

title: Visualise Palettes or Colour Vectors — pal_show
text: palette Character vector palette names (e.g. "lancet"), colour vector (hex codes named colours), NULL show palettes matching pattern/type. Named colour vectors (e.g. pal_paraSC) use valid names labels hex codes missing whitespace-names. Repeated palette names displayed , first-occurrence order; repeated literal colours preserved. Factors, classed vectors, matrices data frames supported. n Positive whole number colours preview palette. Continuous palettes sampled evenly across full range; single colour uses middle palette. Discrete palettes untyped colour vectors take colours front interpolate requested available. max_colors caps many drawn. Default NULL uses native colour count display cap. pattern Single non-missing regex string filter palette names (e.g. "^nord"). Default NULL filter name. type Filter type: "", "discrete", "continuous". max_colors Positive whole number limiting displayed colours per palette, Inf display cap. Default 20. index Non-empty vector unique positive whole-number indices filtering. --range values ignored; empty selection error. output Output format: "gt" (default) gt table, "gg" ggplot, "console" terminal output. label Logical. output = "gg" colour vector mode, whether show hex/name labels tiles. Default TRUE. change gt tables console output. label_size Positive finite number. Tile-label text size output = "gg" colour vector mode. Default 3. ncol Positive whole number columns output = "gg" colour vector mode. Default NULL puts every displayed colour single row.

code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   Type  = factor(sample(c("A","B","C"), 200, TRUE)),   Group = factor(sample(c("X","Y","Z"), 200, TRUE)),   Batch = factor(sample(c("B1","B2"), 200, TRUE)) ) df$Region <- factor(ifelse(df$Group %in% c("X","Y"), "R1", "R2"))  # ===== 1. Bar ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar")                      # stacked %  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar", stat = "count",         position = "dodge")                                      # dodged count  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar", flip = TRUE,         label = TRUE)                                            # flipped + labels  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar", position = "dodge",         bg.by = "Region")                                        # background bands  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar", position = "dodge",         bg.by = "Region",         bg_palette = c("lightblue", "lightyellow"))              # custom bg colors  plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "bar", stat = "count",         label = TRUE, legend.position = "none")                  # no group   # ===== 2. Rose ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "rose")  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "rose", stat = "count",         position = "dodge")   # ===== 3. Ring (donut) ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "ring")  plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "ring", label = TRUE,         palette = "Paired")  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "ring", stat = "count",         position = "dodge")   # ===== 4. Pie ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "pie", label = TRUE)  plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "pie", palette = "Paired",         title = "Type Distribution", subtitle = "n = 200")  plt_cat(df, "Type", type = "pie", legend.position = "bottom",         legend.direction = "horizontal")   # ===== 5. Trend ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "trend", stat = "count")  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "trend", stat = "count",         label = TRUE)   # ===== 6. Area ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "area", stat = "count")  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "area", stat = "count",         position = "dodge")   # ===== 7. Dot ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "dot")  plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "dot", label = TRUE,         stat = "count")   # ===== split.by / NA / keep_empty / aspect ===== plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", split.by = "Batch", type = "bar")  plt_cat(df, "Type", split.by = "Batch", type = "pie",         facet_ncol = 2)   # NA handling df_na <- df; df_na$Type[1:20] <- NA plt_cat(df_na, "Type", "Group", type = "bar",         NA_stat = TRUE, NA_color = "red")   # keep_empty: preserve dropped levels df2 <- df[df$Type != "C", ] plt_cat(df2, "Type", "Group", type = "bar", keep_empty = TRUE)   # aspect.ratio plt_cat(df, "Type", "Group", type = "bar", aspect.ratio = 0.5)   # ===== 8. Sankey ===== plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group"), type = "sankey") #> Warning: attributes are not identical across measure variables; they will be dropped  plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group", "Batch"), type = "sankey") #> Warning: attributes are not identical across measure variables; they will be dropped   # ===== 9. Chord ===== plt_cat(df, c("Type", "Group"), type = "chord")    # ===== 10. Venn ===== set.seed(42) df_bin <- data.frame(   A = sample(c("Yes","No"), 100, TRUE),   B = sample(c("Yes","No"), 100, TRUE),   C = sample(c("Yes","No"), 100, TRUE) ) plt_cat(df_bin, c("A","B","C"), type = "venn")  plt_cat(df, c("Type","Group"), type = "venn", stat_level = c("A","X"))   # ===== 11. UpSet ===== plt_cat(df_bin, c("A","B","C"), type = "upset") #> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0. #> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the ggupset package. #>   Please report the issue at <https://github.com/const-ae/ggupset/issues>.  plt_cat(df, c("Type","Group"), type = "upset", stat_level = c("A","X"))

code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   stage = factor(sample(c("I","II","III","IV"), 200, TRUE)),   sex   = factor(sample(c("M","F"), 200, TRUE)),   race  = factor(sample(c("White","Black","Asian"), 200, TRUE)),   grade = factor(sample(c("Low","Mid","High"), 200, TRUE)) )  # --- Stacked bar (type = "bar") ------------------------------------------- # "count (percent)" labels on one line plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar")   # Count above percent, whole percentages, segments below 10% unlabelled plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",          label_args = list(style = "count_percent_wrap", pct_accuracy = 1,                            min_pct = 0.1))   # Percent-only labels, facets in one column, legend below plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar", facet = "race",          label_args = list(style = "percent"),          facet_args = list(ncol = 1),          legend_args = list(position = "bottom", ncol = 2))   # No labels plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",          label_args = list(style = "none"))   # Registered palette name / literal colour vector plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar", color = "Paired")  plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",          color = c("steelblue", "tomato"))   # Axis titles via fmt_text(); `save = list(filename = "dist.pdf")` would # save this plot plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",          fmt_text = list(xlab = "Stage", ylab = "Percentage"))   # Theme + label size carried by theme_use plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",          theme_use = theme_my(base_size = 16))   # --- Tile heatmap (3 variables; type ignored) ----------------------------- heat_data <- expand.grid(stage = c("I", "II", "III", "IV"),                          grade = c("Low", "Mid", "High")) heat_data$category <- factor(rep(c("A", "B"), 6)) plt_dist(heat_data, dis_vars = c("stage", "grade", "category"))  plt_dist(heat_data, dis_vars = c("stage", "grade", "category"),          label_args = list(style = "none"))   # --- Alluvial flow (default; needs ggalluvial) ---------------------------- if (requireNamespace("ggalluvial", quietly = TRUE)) {   plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"))   plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), facet = "race")   plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"),            label_args = list(style = "count_percent_wrap"))   plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"),            flow_args = list(curve_type = "sigmoid"),            stratum_args = list(width = 0.4, gap = 0.02)) }

Base font family (default "sans"). base_fontface Character. Base font face (default "bold"). base_line_size Numeric. Base line size. base_rect_size Numeric. Base rect size. axis_text_angle Numeric. text: fmt_strip() previously crashed Error: convert call string. applied plot whose first fmt_strip() pass injected synthetic .strip_label. facet. happened -facet branch wrote facet quosure vars(.data[["..."]]) (CALL), -facet branch used rlang::as_name() accepts symbols. Reproducer: patchwork composition sub-plot passed fmt_strip() wrapped, fmt_strip() applied wrapped patchwork (e.g. MLR’s .plt_vd.cat.group_sur .plt_vd.cat.group helpers). public API change; behavior preserved single-pass fmt_strip() usage. text: Companion fct_to_combine(). Collapses factor levels new groups specified integer indices, auto-naming convention g<i1>/<i2>/... (common clinical TNM / RPA staging). Vector API (data parameter), parameter named g_lis:
code: x <- factor(c("I","II","III","IV","V")) fct_to_group(x, list(c(1,3), c(2,4), 5))             # -> g1/3, g2/4, g5 fct_to_group(x, list(early = 1:2, late = 3:5))       # user names win

title: UtilsR 0.6.0
text: Removed data parameter. function now takes vectors directly via ..., aligning forcats::fct_cross() base::interaction(). Migration: Default separator (&) factor-level-ordered output unchanged.
code: # Before (0.5.x and earlier) fct_to_combine(df, sex, age) fct_to_combine(df, c("sex", "age"))  # After (0.6.0+) fct_to_combine(df$sex, df$age) df %>% mutate(g = fct_to_combine(sex, age))           # natural in mutate do.call(fct_to_combine, df[c("sex", "age")])           # programmatic rlang::exec(fct_to_combine, !!!df[c("sex", "age")])    # programmatic (rlang)
